title: Redox
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Redox.

concepts.def: Loss of electrons; oxidation number increases.
Gain of electrons; oxidation number decreases.
A value showing how oxidised an atom is in a species.
Show electron loss or gain at each part of a redox reaction.
Species that accept or donate electrons.
Uses a redox reaction to find an unknown concentration.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Redox — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Redox brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Redox.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The oxidation state of Mn in MnO₄⁻ is:
A cell has E°(cathode) = +0.80 V and E°(anode) = −0.40 V. The EMF is:
What is reduction in terms of electrons?
options: The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.
Gain of electrons (the oxidation number is reduced).
Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.
Reduction means losing oxygen and oxidation means gaining oxygen — full stop.

mcqs.q: In a standard hydrogen electrode used as a reference, what is the assigned electrode potential?
options: The standard hydrogen electrode actually has zero potential because hydrogen has no charge.
The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.
Exactly 0 V by convention — all other electrode potentials are measured relative to it.
Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.

mcqs.q: Is the oxidation state of an atom the same as its actual charge?
options: The oxidation state of an atom is always equal to the number of electrons it has.
Not necessarily — oxidation state is an accounting tool assuming all bonds are fully ionic; real charge is usually smaller.
The oxidation state of an atom is exactly equal to its real ionic charge in every compound.
Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reducing agent”?
options: E°_cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); positive E°_cell indicates a feasible reaction.
Species that donates electrons and is itself oxidised.
Gain of electrons; decrease in oxidation state.
Species that accepts electrons and is itself reduced.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Standard electrode potential E°”?
options: Loss of electrons; increase in oxidation state.
Species that donates electrons and is itself oxidised.
EMF of a half-cell vs standard hydrogen electrode at 298 K, 100 kPa, 1 mol dm⁻³.
Species that accepts electrons and is itself reduced.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Oxidation”?
options: Species that accepts electrons and is itself reduced.
Loss of electrons; increase in oxidation state.
E°_cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); positive E°_cell indicates a feasible reaction.
Species that donates electrons and is itself oxidised.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Electrochemical cell EMF”?
options: EMF of a half-cell vs standard hydrogen electrode at 298 K, 100 kPa, 1 mol dm⁻³.
E°_cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); positive E°_cell indicates a feasible reaction.
Gain of electrons; decrease in oxidation state.
Loss of electrons; increase in oxidation state.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Oxidising agent”?
options: Gain of electrons; decrease in oxidation state.
Species that donates electrons and is itself oxidised.
Species that accepts electrons and is itself reduced.
EMF of a half-cell vs standard hydrogen electrode at 298 K, 100 kPa, 1 mol dm⁻³.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reduction”?
options: EMF of a half-cell vs standard hydrogen electrode at 298 K, 100 kPa, 1 mol dm⁻³.
Loss of electrons; increase in oxidation state.
Gain of electrons; decrease in oxidation state.
E°_cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); positive E°_cell indicates a feasible reaction.
